analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/operations/provider-release.md. Visible changes: date bump, a rename of qualify-sdk to qualify-sdk-shard at head line 299, and a new statement at head ~564-568 that qualify-sdk passes only when all five shard jobs pass and together executed the full provider suite. The remaining changed-range edits (head 579-581, 604-606, 609-612, 651-792) are mostly shifts from the added lines; I saw no substantive semantic edits in the supplied text. I identified no change to code, workflows, keys, attestation policy, authorization or trust boundaries, so TB-011, TB-002 and T-053/T-054 behavior is unchanged.

The doc describes the dev-branch lane (the `release-dev-branch.yml` caller, which uses secrets: inherit and signs dev builds with the production Developer ID). It records that review is not enforced on `dev` and that a pull_request rule is required before the lane runs. The doc itself states this open gap and the production gating: dev builds satisfy the self-updater DarkbloomCodeSignature requirement, and only production registration and the production release key keep a dev build out of production. Those controls are described, not changed here. Whether the actual workflows enforce this (the environment == 'prod' guards, the ruleset on dev, the `scripts/provider-release-resume.py` source gate) is outside the supplied evidence and unverified; the doc is not evidence of a regression. Next pass should check that release-dev-branch.yml and release-provider.yml match the documented secret guards and that the dev-branch pull_request rule is actually added. The shard-gating claim also needs verification against release-provider.yml, since a gate that is not wired as described would weaken the SDK qualification before signing. No finding is warranted from the docs alone.
